author: kevaundray
content:
I think the following invariant would be nice to have: whichever key the CL is using for validator duties, is the key that deposits/topups can be made against.

This means that if the CL is using BLS, then we can only use the old BLS deposit contract to do topups. Then once we have moved over to PQ, then one can only make deposits/topups against PQ credentials

author: kevaundray
content: The front-running issue you mention is a problem today for Lido, which is why signatures/proof-of-possession is usually required

author: kevaundray
content: There is a way to not require proof of possession and allow duplicate keys for a validator, but its more invasive and has an annoying edge case related to committee selection

author: terencechain
content:
yeah agreed on that invariant, but i think my question is slightly different. even if we only accept PQ keys after the fork, someone can still deposit with my key and their withdrawal address before my pre-reg gets included . should we require an active matching pre-reg for the first deposit
i also understand pre-reg gets rejected if there exists a pending deposit (assuming attackers), this is good, but operator really needs to be careful here

author: kevaundray
content:
Personally I think so.

Though just to clarify, there a few contracts (I'll rename for my own clarity):

- pq migration contract: This is the contract that will be used by existing validators to register PQ material against their BLS key

- pre-registration contract: This is basically Lido style 8205 and it stops the operator from frontrunning the staker when they both know the private key for operator public key

- pq deposit contract: This is the new deposit contract that will accept PQ deposits and topups

author: kevaundray
content: The pre-registration contract is a confusing name because I think we also use that to mean the pq migration contract at certain points in time
